description: Statically derived by reading app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl, never captured from a run: the COBOL cannot be executed in this environment, so every byte below is taken from the source, the copybooks and the fixture rather than from an execution log (risk R-A, practice B12). No user rules govern this file - review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided.' - so it is held to enterprise best practice instead, and the practices it leans on are named where they apply. This case completes the three-arm set over the ordered EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :1392: case06.json takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :1393 from genuinely seeded data, case07.json takes WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :1395 from a key the fixture does not hold, and this case takes WHEN OTHER at :1402 - the arm reached only after the first two have both been passed over, which is gate G30, and the third and last of this program's READ outcomes, which is gate G47. The scenario is case06's exactly: EIBCALEN 489, AID ENTER, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equal to LIT-CCLISTPGM 'COCRDLIC' (:227-228) and CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, so the :388-401 guard fails both limbs of its IF and takes the ELSE at :396-400, slicing CARDDEMO-COMMAREA from DFHCOMMAREA(1:160) and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA from DFHCOMMAREA(161:329) so the inbound account and card ids survive; ENTER is admitted unchanged by :413-424 because :414 lists CCARD-AID-ENTER; and the ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :429 passes over arm one (:435-439, PF03 and the two done/failed arms, all false) to match arm two's first WHEN at :482-483, which sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :486, INPUT-OK at :487, both filter flags ISVALID at :488-489, moves CDEMO-ACCT-ID and CDEMO-CARD-NUM into the numeric REDEFINES views CC-ACCT-ID-N and CC-CARD-NUM-N at :490-491, performs 9000-READ-DATA at :492-493, sets CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :494, performs 3000-SEND-MAP at :495-496 and leaves through GO TO COMMON-RETURN at :497. One thing differs from case06: the CARDDAT read is driven to an unexpected RESP. That RESP is INJECTED DELIBERATELY (practice B1), because no fixture row can produce one - a seeded slice can hold the key (case06) or not hold it (case07), but it cannot make EXEC CICS READ answer something else. The repository is therefore driven through the common/FileStatus 'other' outcome, declared here as forcedOutcomes.read with outcome OTHER, resp 19 and resp2 0. Nineteen is DFHRESP(NOTOPEN), a file that is defined but not open, which is precisely the class of failure this arm exists to report; both numbers are pinned constants rather than anything derived from the environment, because they appear VERBATIM in the message text, and they are the same pair the sibling file-error cases pin (COCRDSLC/case19.json, COTRN02C/case10.json) so the set stays comparable across programs. WHEN OTHER's body at :1403-1411 is five statements and one guard, and the guard sits in a structurally odd place. SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE at :1403 is unguarded. IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :1404 then guards SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :1405 - the guard tests the MESSAGE field while what it protects is a FIELD FLAG, and it protects only the account filter, never the card filter. The four MOVEs that assemble the message and the MOVE that delivers it, :1407 through :1411, are then entirely UNGUARDED. The asymmetry is real, it is preserved rather than tidied (practice B5) and it is recorded rather than papered over (practice B4): the NOTFND arm immediately above does the exact opposite, setting BOTH filter flags unguarded at :1397-1398 and guarding its MESSAGE at :1399-1401. The consequence on this path is that the file-error text OVERWRITES whatever message was already sitting in WS-RETURN-MSG, so a program that had already told the user something specific loses that text to the file error, while the field flag that would have marked the offending field is the part that gets suppressed. Here WS-RETURN-MSG is still SPACES from SET WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :384, so both limbs fire: FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set and the message is written. That trace is what the attributes rest on, and it was reasoned out from the two SET sites rather than assumed from the mere fact that a read failed: :488-489 had set BOTH filters ISVALID and WHEN OTHER touches only the account one, so FLG-CARDFILTER remains ISVALID, :1243-1245 moves DFHRED into ACCTSIDC and :1253-1255 does NOT move it into CARDSIDC. That single byte is the whole observable difference between this case and case07.json, where NOTFND reddens both search keys. THE HEADLINE FINDING is an 80-byte message moved into a 75-byte field. WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE at :133-152 is nine items whose widths sum mechanically (practice B11): FILLER X(12) 'File Error: ' at 1-12, ERROR-OPNAME X(8) at 13-20, FILLER X(4) ' on ' at 21-24, ERROR-FILE X(9) at 25-33, FILLER X(15) ' returned RESP ' at 34-48, ERROR-RESP X(10) at 49-58, FILLER X(7) ',RESP2 ' at 59-65, ERROR-RESP2 X(10) at 66-75, and a trailing FILLER X(5) at 76-80 - 12+8+4+9+15+10+7+10+5 = 80. The receiver is WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) at :173, and a COBOL MOVE between alphanumeric items truncates on the RIGHT, so five bytes are lost. Laying the offsets out identifies them exactly rather than by eye: 12+8+4+9+15+10+7 = 65 puts ERROR-RESP2 at 66-75, so the 75-byte prefix ends precisely on ERROR-RESP2's last byte and the five bytes that fall off ARE that trailing FILLER. ERROR-RESP2 survives intact at the field's tail and nothing informative is lost. 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG then does MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO ERRMSGO at :1163, and ERRMSGO is PIC X(80) in app/cpy-bms/COCRDUP.CPY:212, so the 75 bytes are re-padded with five spaces and ERRMSGO is asserted at exactly 80. Stated honestly, because it matters more than the truncation itself: since the five lost bytes were spaces and the re-pad restores spaces, the 80 to 75 to 80 round trip is OBSERVATIONALLY NEUTRAL on this path - ERRMSGO comes out byte-identical to the 80-byte source image. The assertion is still not vacuous, because it discriminates the failures that would actually occur. A translation truncating the WRONG end would drop 'File ' and shift ERROR-RESP2 into 61-70, changing every byte from 61 to 80. One omitting the trailing FILLER while composing would produce 75 characters where 80 are declared. One trimming the receiver would produce 74. Each is caught. What is NOT caught, and is said here rather than left to be discovered, is a translation that pads to 80 before the move instead of truncating to 75 and re-padding: on this path the two are indistinguishable, and the 75-byte width is pinned instead by COMMON-RETURN's MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO CCARD-ERROR-MSG at :547, whose receiver is the PIC X(75) of app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy and which travels back in the payload. The field contents are read from source. ERROR-OPNAME receives the literal 'READ' at :1407 into X(8), giving 'READ' followed by four spaces. ERROR-FILE receives LIT-CARDFILENAME at :1408, declared PIC X(8) VALUE 'CARDDAT ' at :251-252, into an X(9) field, giving 'CARDDAT' followed by two spaces - one from the literal's own trailing byte and one from the receiver being a byte wider. ERROR-RESP and ERROR-RESP2 receive WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD at :1409-1410, and both are PIC S9(09) COMP at :41-44, so these are binary-to-alphanumeric MOVEs: the value is rendered as its nine-digit unsigned zoned DISPLAY string and then moved as alphanumeric into PIC X(10), left-justified and space-padded on the right. 19 therefore renders '000000019' plus one pad space and 0 renders '000000000' plus one pad space - nine digits and not ten, with the tenth byte padding rather than a leading zero, which is the reasoning most likely to be got wrong by inspection. The composed 80 bytes are byte-identical to the ERRMSGO already committed in COCRDSLC/case19.json, whose WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE is the same declaration; two files derived independently agreeing byte for byte is worth more than either alone. This file also records the G47 BOUNDARY for COCRDUPC. The three arms above are the whole of this program's READ outcome space: there is NO '10' end-of-file outcome and NO '22' duplicate outcome anywhere in COCRDUPC, because the program performs no browse, no WRITE and no ADD. Its only file verbs are EXEC CICS READ at :1382, EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :1427 and EXEC CICS REWRITE at :1477, and card.CardRepository deliberately defines neither an add nor a delete. G47 is satisfied for this program by these three 9100 arms plus the two binary checks in 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING that cases 18 and 19 carry, and not by inventing status values the program cannot reach. Gate G45 is satisfied by a negative fact worth recording. LIT-CARDFILENAME-ACCT-PATH PIC X(8) VALUE 'CARDAIX ' is declared at :253-254 and, verified by exhaustive search, never referenced again; both MOVEs to WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID are commented out, at :1379 in 9100 and :1424 in 9200. COCRDUPC therefore NEVER reads the alternate-index path, no CARDAIX access is declared here and none is expected. CARDAIX is an additional finder method on the single card.CardRepository, never a second repository and never a second table, and this program does not call it. THE 2000-DECIDE-ACTION ABEND is recorded here as the folder's single witness, derived byte for byte. Its ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :949 has seven arms before WHEN OTHER: (a) WHEN CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED at :954 carries NO BODY and falls into (b) WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK12 at :958, whose body reads the card file only IF both filters are ISVALID; (c) WHEN CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :971; (d) WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :982; (e) WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED AND CCARD-AID-PFK05 at :988-989; (f) the BARE WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED at :1006, which is why (e) must be tested first; and (g) WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE at :1011. Reaching WHEN OTHER at :1019 needs CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION to hold a byte matched by none of them, which given the 88-levels at :276-290 - LOW-VALUES or SPACES, 'S', 'E', 'N', 'C', 'L', 'F' - means a byte outside that alphabet, and it needs CCARD-AID-PFK12 false. The state byte can only be out of alphabet because it ARRIVES FROM THE INBOUND PAYLOAD, restored from DFHCOMMAREA(161:329) at :398-400, which is exactly why gate G37 matters. The full reachability is stricter than the state byte alone, and this is the part easiest to get wrong: 2000 is performed only from the main EVALUATE's own WHEN OTHER at :535-542, so arm two must miss, which needs CDEMO-PGM-REENTER inbound and an AID that is neither PFK12 nor PFK03; and 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS runs first at :536-537, so 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS must leave the state byte ALONE. At :645 IF CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED fails, :663 CONTINUEs, :668-670 set FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT and both filters ISVALID, and :680-683 compare FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA) with FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(CCUP-OLD-CARDDATA); only when those match does :682 SET NO-CHANGES-DETECTED and :685-693 GO TO the exit WITHOUT touching CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION. Otherwise :696 SETs CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK and 2000 takes arm (d) instead. So the construction is: inbound state byte outside the alphabet, CDEMO-PGM-REENTER, AID ENTER, and received map data equal to the inbound CCUP-OLD-CARDDATA snapshot. WHEN OTHER's body at :1020-1026 then MOVEs LIT-THISPGM to ABEND-CULPRIT giving 'COCRDUPC' at X(8), '0001' to ABEND-CODE at X(4), SPACES to ABEND-REASON at X(50) and the 24-character 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' to ABEND-MSG at X(72), and performs ABEND-ROUTINE THRU ABEND-ROUTINE-EXIT. In ABEND-ROUTINE at :1531-1553 the IF ABEND-MSG EQUAL LOW-VALUES guard at :1533 does NOT fire, because ABEND-MSG already holds that specific text, so 'UNEXPECTED ABEND OCCURRED.' is never substituted and the specific text survives; :1537 then MOVEs LIT-THISPGM to ABEND-CULPRIT a SECOND time, which is redundant and is preserved rather than removed (practice B5); and :1539-1552 issues EXEC CICS SEND FROM(ABEND-DATA) LENGTH(LENGTH OF ABEND-DATA) NOHANDLE ERASE, then EXEC CICS HANDLE ABEND CANCEL, then EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE('9999'). ABEND-DATA is app/cpy/CSMSG02Y.cpy:21-29 and its widths sum mechanically (practice B11) to ABEND-CODE X(4) at 1-4 plus ABEND-CULPRIT X(8) at 5-12 plus ABEND-REASON X(50) at 13-62 plus ABEND-MSG X(72) at 63-134, which is 4+8+50+72 = 134, so the sent image is '0001' then 'COCRDUPC' then fifty spaces then 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' padded to 72, and the ABCODE is '9999'. That derivation is recorded in this description rather than declared in expectedMessages, and the reason is a fact about the source and about the case contract rather than a shortcut. The two arms are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE inside one invocation: 9000-READ-DATA is performed at exactly two sites, :492 in main arm two - which ends GO TO COMMON-RETURN at :497, so 2000 is unreachable from it - and :961 inside 2000's arm (b), which is not WHEN OTHER; ABEND-ROUTINE is performed at exactly one site, :1025, on a path that reads no card file at all and so produces no file-error message; and the abend precedes 3000-SEND-MAP at :540, so that path sends no map either. The ParityCase wire contract carries exactly ONE invocation - one screenRequest, with sends a list only because a program may SEND more than once WITHIN one invocation - so no single case can traverse both, and declaring an ABEND-DATA line that this run cannot emit would guarantee a non-zero diff and defeat gate G18. The derivation is therefore kept complete and auditable here, in the same way case06.json records 2000-DECIDE-ACTION as not reached, and a case built on the construction named above can assert it directly on the DISPLAY_LINE channel at 134 characters. Gate G35 DOES NOT APPLY to this program at all, and that is recorded rather than silently omitted: COCRDUPC contains ZERO occurrences of CALL 'CEE3ABD', so there is no Language Environment abend to map to a RETURN-CODE. It abends through EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE('9999') at :1550-1552, which is a CICS transaction abend and not a batch return code, so the abend is expressed through the message text and the common/AbendException shape and NEVER by putting a non-zero value in expectedReturnCode, which stays 0. The screen consequences follow 3000-SEND-MAP's fixed order at :1036-1045 - 3100, then 3200, then 3250, then 3300, then 3400 - and that order is load-bearing twice over. 3100-SCREEN-INIT fills CCRDUPAO with LOW-VALUES at :1053 and then writes the two active COTTL01Y titles, LIT-THISTRANID, LIT-THISPGM and the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS renderings of the pinned clock. 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS runs its ELSE limb at :1086-1133 because :486 flipped the context to REENTER; CC-ACCT-ID-N and CC-CARD-NUM-N are both non-zero so ACCTSIDO and CARDSIDO carry the ids at X(11) and X(16), and the inner four-arm ordered EVALUATE at :1099 passes over arm one (:1100, CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, false now that :494 made the state 'S') to match arm two at :1107-1112, which paints CRDNAMEO, CRDSTCDO, EXPDAYO, EXPMONO and EXPYEARO from CCUP-OLD-*. Those five come out BLANK, and that is the read failure made visible: 9000-READ-DATA INITIALIZEd CCUP-OLD-DETAILS at :1345 and moved only the two ids into it at :1346-1347, and because FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT is false the IF at :1352-1369 never ran, so the CVV, the folded embossed name, the three sliced date parts and the active status were never taken. INITIALIZE leaves alphanumeric items at SPACES, so CRDNAMEO is fifty spaces, CRDSTCDO one, EXPMONO and EXPDAYO two each and EXPYEARO four - identical to case07.json, which is correct, because a read that found nothing and a read that failed leave the same empty snapshot. 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG is ordered the same way: arm one at :1141 CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is false, arm two at :1143 CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is false, arm three at :1145-1146 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS matches, so SET FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT puts the :160-161 literal into WS-INFO-MSG and INFOMSGO reads 'Details of selected card shown above' padded to X(40); :1163 then delivers the truncated file-error text into the X(80) ERRMSGO. The screen therefore says the card details are shown above WHILE reporting that the read failed and showing five empty fields. That contradiction is noted honestly rather than resolved (practice B5): the state byte drives the info message and the RESP drives the error message, and nothing in the program reconciles them. Gate G38, the highlight, is asserted against the program's own statements, because COCRDUPC does NOT COPY CSSETATY - that logic is inline at :1243-1307. Exactly one DFHRED is written, into ACCTSIDC at :1244, from the FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK that the guarded SET at :1405 did set; CARDSIDC keeps the DFHDFCOL that :1240 wrote, because FLG-CARDFILTER is still ISVALID. Not one '*' can appear: the two '*' paths at :1247-1251 and :1257-1261 require FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK or FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK, which is the ' ' value and not the '0' value that NOT-OK carries, and the four data-field paths from :1263 to :1307 each additionally require CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, which is 'E', while the state here is 'S'. The :1238-1241 arm is taken, since CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is the 'COCRDLI' that COCRDLIC left there, and it moves DFHDFCOL into both search-key colours - which for ACCTSIDC is then overwritten two lines later, a genuine branch whose effect survives on one field and not the other. The 3300 protection matrix matches the arm group at :1181-1190 for state 'S': DFHBMPRF to ACCTSIDA and CARDSIDA, the two search keys becoming protected now that they have been used, and DFHBMFSE to CRDNAMEA, CRDSTCDA, EXPMONA and EXPYEARA, with EXPDAYA commented out at :1185; :1285 moves DFHBMDAR into EXPDAYC unconditionally; and :1309-1313 moves DFHBMBRY into INFOMSGA because WS-INFO-MSG is not blank. Those land on xxxA items, which are the attribute REDEFINES of the xxxF flag bytes on the input map, so they are recorded in this description, which is the audit trail, while the attributes member carries the seventeen xxxC colour items the send actually paints - sixteen at DFHDFCOL apart from ACCTSIDC at DFHRED, with EXPDAYC at DFHBMDAR from :1285. The names are common/BmsAttributes constants. :1315-1317 leaves FKEYSCA alone, because PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION is false. The cursor EVALUATE at :1211-1235 is ordered and writes exactly one -1, and this is the sharpest G30 assertion in the file: arm one at :1212-1214 tests FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT, which 3250 set one paragraph earlier, so it wins BY SOURCE ORDER over the FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK arm at :1215-1217 that the flag state would otherwise select, and -1 goes into CRDNAMEL and nowhere else. The cursor rests on the card name even though the account field is the one painted red. A translation that evaluated the flags first would put the cursor on ACCTSIDL and pass every other assertion in this file. xxxL is metadata expressed as the cursor and never as a payload member. No next program is named: CCARD-NEXT-PROG is assigned only at :570 inside 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS, which arm two never performs, while 3400-SEND-SCREEN does assign CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET and CCARD-NEXT-MAP at :1326-1327, so the response carries the mapset and the map but no program, and the transaction ends on the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(LIT-THISTRANID) of COMMON-RETURN at :554-558. Gate G37: the whole conversation state travels in the payload - the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus the 329-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, which is 1 + 89 + 89 + 150 and which :549-557 concatenates, for the declared EIBCALEN of 489 - and none of it is held server-side, so CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT returns as 1 from :486 while every other commarea field echoes the inbound value, the WHEN OTHER arm writing none of them. The unit is card.CardUpdateController driven as a plain object through its single entry point, with no MockMvc and no HTTP anywhere in the path, which is gate G51; jobParameters is empty because a controller takes none. NOTHING IS WRITTEN on this path: the run attempts one read, fails it, and sends one map, so expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty as positive assertions that no record was written and no dataset mutated, rather than by omission, and no dataset expectation is declared on either channel. expectedMessages is empty for the same reason - the program emits no DISPLAY and no unformatted text on this path, only the map, which is asserted in sends. It is correctly never a thank-you or an invalid-key literal: CSMSG01Y's CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU and CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY have ZERO references in COCRDUPC, and only CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 are used, at :1057-1058. Those two titles are byte-exact from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, where line 21 is COMMENTED OUT, so TITLE02O carries the ACTIVE line 22 'CardDemo' text at X(40) and not the commented 'Credit Card Demo Application (CCDA)' text. The seed is genuine fixture data (gate G16): rows 1 to 3 of fixtures/carddata.txt, which is byte-identical to app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt, the same slice case06.json uses so the two cases differ only in the forced outcome. Row 1 decodes at the CVACT02Y offsets as CARD-NUM [1-16] '0500024453765740', CARD-ACCT-ID [17-27] '00000000050', CARD-CVV-CD [28-30] '747', CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME [31-80] 'Aniya Von' padded to 50, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE [81-90] '2023-03-09' - the copybook's own misspelling, preserved verbatim, because renaming it would break field-for-field diffing - CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS [91] 'Y' and FILLER [92-150] fifty-nine spaces, the widths summing to 16+11+3+50+10+1+59 = 150, which is gate G19. The forced outcome means the seed is never actually read, and that is stated rather than left implicit. No normalisation is declared because carddata.txt already ships at its full copybook width; only cardxref.txt needs the 36-to-50 pad. The clock is pinned to this source's own version footer, 2022-07-19 23:12:33, so CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are assertable at all and the case is deterministic (practices B7 and B9); the charset is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). Gate G32 is not encoded because all twenty-one GO TOs in this program are forward, and gate G39 is not encoded because this screen does not paginate.

fields.INFOMSGO: Details of selected card shown above
fields.ERRMSGO: File Error: READ     on CARDDAT   returned RESP 000000019 ,RESP2 000000000
